description: MACRO (NEW 4th worker; OPERATOR SYNTHESIS — the aggressive GEMM-only solver half) — BUILD a working CholeskyQR2 + ORHR_COL n512 solver in submission.py that emits EXACT flat (H,tau) and beats the serial-Householder path on WELL-CONDITIONED DENSE n512. This is the panel-killing aggressive algorithm; W1 is concurrently building the structure-PROBE that will route benign matrices to your solver — you build the SOLVER, W1 builds the gate; they compose. THE ALGORITHM: G = A^T A (one big compute-bound tensor-core GEMM — tf32 now, FP4 later); R = cholesky(G); Q = A @ R^-1 (triangular solve / trsm); ONE reorthogonalization pass (CholeskyQR2: repeat G2=Q^T Q, R2=chol(G2), Q=Q R2^-1, R=R2 R) for stability; then ORHR_COL reconstruction to recover the FLAT geqrf (H,tau) the checker requires (Q=householder_product(tril(H,-1),tau), R=triu(H)). PROVEN PRECEDENT: prior commit d60e14e6 already implemented ORHR_COL reconstruction that VALIDATED 22/22 — find it (git show d60e14e6) and REUSE/adapt its reconstruction machinery; do not reinvent. SCOPE: gate your new path to N==512 AND a benign condition (start: hardcode it ON only for the dense-cond test batches to prove it out, then W1's probe will supply the real gate). BUILD IT FOR REAL in submission.py, build+validate+benchmark via autocuda run. FIRST MILESTONE: get CholeskyQR2+ORHR_COL VALIDATING (factor residual + orthogonality + diff-guard PASS) on the n512 dense/dense-cond2 batches, then confirm it BEATS the Householder path's n512 time there (it should — no serial panel, pure GEMM). Then push precision down (tf32 Gram -> FP4 Gram via _scaled_mm_v2, the regime where FP4 is fast AND accurate on cond~1). NO STOPPING / NO ESCAPE HATCHES: if the first reconstruction is wrong or slow, fix it and iterate; try variants (2 vs 3 CholeskyQR passes, Gram precision, trsm vs explicit inverse, reconstruction tiling) until it ships a win. Only modify the real submission.py via autocuda run; NO isolated microbenchmarks; NO comment-only commits. Keep H,tau packed-exact. NO stream substring. nvidia-smi~0 SYNC, rank LOCAL. Fork 864c6e52 (best 2371.7us). Distinct from W1 (probe/gate), W2 (n512 trailing correction), W0 (large-n FP4). Submit if beat 2371.7us. Goal under 1000us = beat #1.

CholeskyQR2+orhr_col n512 solver VALIDATES 22/22 + all guards (diff-correctness, invariance batch/fraction/position sweeps CLEAN). GEMM-only G=A^T A + chol + A R^-1 + 1 reortho pass + orhr_col flat (H,tau), per-matrix Householder fallback for ill-cond. NOT a perf win yet: blocked no-pivot LU per-column Python loop (512 tiny launches/matrix at n512) dominates -> 102ms/n512-shape, geomean 6861us vs baseline 2371. Algorithm proven correct; next replace LU loop with on-chip Triton diag-block factorization.

CholeskyQR2+orhr_col with OWN diag_lu + tri_inv NVRTC kernels (replace cuSOLVER batched solve_triangular, the n512 wall). diag_lu: on-chip no-pivot LU of diag block (one batch launch, kills per-col Python loop). tri_inv: on-chip triangular-block inverse + recursive 2x2 block driver -> Rinv via bmm; Q=A@Rinv pure bmm. Plus column equilibration + tf32x3 bmm helper. VALIDATES 22/22 + guards at fp32. NOT a perf win: fp32 SIMT slow -> n512 43ms, geomean 5205 vs base 2371. KEY MEASURED FINDING: benchmark dense-cond2 has cond(G)~5e11 -> Gram needs ~fp64 (tf32x3 goes indefinite, cholesky fails). NEXT: int-Ozaki exact-fp64 Gram on tensor cores.

shifted-CholeskyQR3 + tf32x3 everywhere + strict per-matrix orth gate. VALIDATES 22/22 + guards. Shift makes the tf32x3 Gram's cholesky succeed on high-cond(An); x3 reconstruction LU keeps householder_product orthogonal; strict orth-residual gate falls back non-orthogonal matrices. DIAG: dense-cond2 routes 15-16/16 through CholeskyQR3 at orth ~4.5e-6. NOT a perf win yet: x3 (3 GEMMs/op) x3 passes + x3 recon LU is GEMM-heavy -> n512 71ms (75% contended), geomean 6134. NEXT cut GEMM count: drop non-critical ops to tf32, fewer passes, cheaper recon.

orhr_col tau from reflector-norm relation tau=2/(v^Tv) instead of LU pivots -> reconstructed reflectors EXACTLY orthogonal regardless of LU precision, so recon LU runs cheap single-tf32 (only loose factor residual sees LU precision). VALIDATES 22/22+guards. Recon tf32 (71->68ms) but 3-pass x3 CholeskyQR3 Gram+applies are the wall. geomean 6037. CONCLUSION: tf32x3 (3 GEMMs/op) makes CQR3 ~comparable to whole optimized Householder kernel; FP4 (4x, #1's approach) needed to win.

Gate CholeskyQR3 OFF by default (QR_CQR2_N512=0): branch is now perf-neutral (geomean 2374.9 == baseline 2375, n512 4240us == Householder) and combinable, with the validated CholeskyQR3+orhr_col machinery preserved behind the flag. The tf32x3 path is correct but ~16x slower than Householder; FP4 needed to win.

Last reortho pass at single tf32 (orth ~4e-4 << gate 3e-3, dense-cond2 still 15-16/16). Saves one x3 pass (68->60ms route ON). Route default OFF (perf-neutral, geomean=baseline). KEY FINDING: tf32 bmm at B=640,n=512 = 0.33ms, so FLOP budget allows a win (~10 ops ~3ms < Householder 4.2ms); current 60ms is STRUCTURAL OVERHEAD (recursive triinv small-GEMMs x3, per-panel recon .contiguous copies, full-NxN tril/triu+.double traffic) + x3, not FLOPs. Win path = lean reimpl (fused x3 GEMM, batched triinv, fused single-kernel recon).

BUILT a complete, VALIDATED CholeskyQR3 + orhr_col GEMM-only n512 solver (brief-0, 6 commits, HEAD dbdc8cab on worker-3 branch). It validates 22/22 + diff-correctness + invariance guards and correctly routes the dense-cond2 majority (15-16/16 matrices) through the GEMM path at orth ~4e-4 (gate 3e-3), falling the rest back to Householder via a strict per-matrix orth gate. NEW DURABLE MACHINERY (NVRTC kernels added to _CUDA_SRC): diag_lu (on-chip no-pivot LU of the diag block with the diag-D pivot regularization), tri_inv (on-chip triangular-block inverse) + recursive blocked driver; shifted-CholeskyQR3 (shift makes the tf32x3 Gram's cholesky succeed on high-cond(An)); orhr_col with tau=2/(v^Tv) (reflectors EXACTLY orthogonal regardless of LU precision -> recon runs cheap tf32); column equilibration. NOT YET A WIN: ~14-16x SLOWER than Householder on n512 (60ms vs 4.2ms). Route is gated OFF by default so the branch is PERF-NEUTRAL (geomean 2374.87 == baseline 2375) and combinable; machinery stays behind QR_CQR2_N512=1. KEY MEASURED FINDINGS for the next brief: (1) a single tf32 bmm at B=640,n=512 is only 0.33ms, so the FLOP budget DOES allow a win (~10-15 GEMM-ops ~3-5ms < Householder 4.2ms) -- this is NOT fundamentally walled. (2) The 60ms is STRUCTURAL OVERHEAD, not FLOPs: the tf32x3 emulation allocates ~6 full-size (670MB) temporaries per call (~15ms of pure memory traffic across the pipeline), _cqr2_triinv's recursive 2x2 inverse spawns dozens of small x3 GEMMs (called 3x), the orhr_col reconstruction does 8 sequential panels with per-panel .contiguous copies, and there are full-NxN tril/triu+.double() passes. (3) The dense-cond2 intrinsic cond(An)~1.8e3 median (4.7e5 max) FORCES 3 CholeskyQR passes at tf32x3 (cond > u^{-1/2}=1000 for x3); fp32 (u^{-1/2}=3000) would allow 2 passes but fp32 bmm is 9x slower (SIMT). WIN PATH (recommend a fresh brief): a LEAN reimplementation -- (a) a FUSED tf32x3 GEMM (Triton, compute hi/lo splits + accumulate in one kernel, zero temporaries) to kill the ~15ms memory overhead; (b) replace _cqr2_triinv for the well-conditioned reortho passes (R2~=I) with a 2-3-term Neumann/Newton-Schulz inverse (1-2 bmms instead of dozens); (c) a fused single-kernel orhr_col reconstruction (avoid the 8-panel Python orchestration). Alternatively FP4 (NVFP4 _scaled_mm exists but is 2D-only -> needs batched-friendly packing) as the #1-leader path, but my probe shows FP4 needs custom batching and its extreme low precision needs Ozaki correction (uncertain net win). HANDOFF to W0: my diag_lu uses piv = diag - sign(diag) which is EXACTLY the pivot regularization that fixes W0's n4096 orhr_col NaN (near-zero leading minors); W0 can reuse diag_lu/tri_inv from this branch.

Newton-Schulz reortho (1 chol + NS steps, R=Q^TA recovered once) + section-timing. SECTION-TIMING (n512 B=640, the key result): reortho 26-28ms (41%, the wall), gate 11, gram 4.6, chol 4, triinv1 4.8, recon 7.5, equil 2.6 = ~64ms. NS does NOT beat cholesky reortho -- both ~26ms because each needs ~2 full-NxN x3 bmms and orthogonalization needs 4-6. tf32-NS floors orth at 9e-3 > checker gate 6e-3 so NS must be x3. 1chol+2 x3-NS routes 91% at orth 1e-5. CONCLUSION (fully measured): tf32x3 CholeskyQR3 CANNOT beat Householder 4.2ms -- the ~4-6 full-NxN x3 reortho bmms are a ~26ms wall; single tf32 bmm is 0.33ms but x3 is required for PD/orthogonality. Win needs FP4 (4x) + correction. Route default OFF (perf-neutral 2374.87).

Pursued the lean reimplementation EXHAUSTIVELY (8 commits, HEAD e85e9dcf, worker-3 branch). Drove n512 CQR3 from 102ms -> 60ms but it remains ~14x slower than Householder (4.2ms), and SECTION-TIMING now proves the gap is NOT removable overhead -- it is the x3 GEMM precision requirement, an algorithmic constraint. MEASURED EVERYTHING the brief asked for: (1) FUSED tf32x3 Triton GEMM (tl.dot input_precision=tf32x3, zero temporaries) -- SLOWER than torch's 3 cublas GEMMs (91 vs 65ms): cublas is so optimized that 3 of its GEMMs + memory beat one Triton kernel, so the overhead is NOT the x3 temporaries' memory traffic. (2) NEWTON-SCHULZ reortho (1 cholesky to enter the basin + NS steps, R=Q^T A recovered once) -- NS does NOT beat cholesky reortho: BOTH cost ~26ms because each needs ~2 full-NxN x3 bmms and orthogonalization needs 4-6 of them; tf32-NS is cheap but floors orth at 9e-3, OVER the 6e-3 checker gate, so NS must be x3. (3) SECTION-TIMING (env QR_CQR2_TIME=1, n512 B=640): reortho 26ms (the wall), gate 11ms, recon 7.5ms, gram/chol/triinv1/equil/apply1 ~18ms = ~64ms. (4) fp16 probe: fp16 bmm is 1.8x faster than tf32 (0.18 vs 0.33ms) BUT fp16x3 relerr floors at 4.6e-4 (~= fp16x1) -- fp16's 5-bit exponent + accumulation kills the hi/lo split, so fp16 is NOT accurate enough for the Gram (needs ~1e-7) or orthogonality. DEFINITIVE CONCLUSION: a single tf32 bmm at B=640,n=512 is only 0.33ms, but the algorithm REQUIRES tf32x3 (the ONLY fast B200 GEMM that keeps the high-cond Gram PD and reaches the orth gate; fp16x3 floors at 5e-4, FP4 is worse), and CholeskyQR3 needs ~4-6 full-NxN x3 reortho bmms = ~26ms irreducible >> Householder 4.2ms. STRATEGIC FINDING: n512 is precisely where Householder is STRONGEST (grid-saturated at B=640, ~2% SM-throughput headroom, well-tuned kernels); CholeskyQR's GEMM-throughput advantage only materializes at LARGER n (n1024/n4096) where Householder's SERIAL PANEL dominates -- i.e. W0's domain. RECOMMEND: do NOT keep grinding n512 CQR (the x3 wall is real and measured); instead point the validated CQR3 machinery at n1024/n4096 where the FLOP budget + Householder's serial-panel weakness favor it, and where the operator's FP4 work (4x GEMMs + Ozaki correction) can finally close the precision-vs-speed gap. But n1024 is the OPPOSITE regime: B=60 < 148 SMs so Householder is GRID-STARVED, its serial panel is ~50% of n1024 (the weakness CQR's all-GEMM structure exploits), and n1024 = 26.6% of geomean. Applied the validated CQR3 machinery to n1024 (brief-1, 3 commits, HEAD 4b9024e1). It VALIDATES 22/22 + guards and routes the n1024 dense majority (~40-45/60), but CANNOT beat Householder, for a QUANTITATIVELY CLEAR reason. THE CROSSOVER ANALYSIS (the key result): CQR3's cost is ~constant ~20-38ms across n512/n1024/n2048/n4096 because the GEMM FLOPs are batch*n^3 and these shapes all have batch*n^3 ~ 1e11 (n512 B=640, n1024 B=60, n2048 B=8, n4096 B=2). Householder, by contrast, scales with grid-starvation: n512=4243us, n1024=3824us, n2048=8634us, n4096=31308us. So CQR3 beats Householder ONLY where Householder exceeds ~20ms -- i.e. n4096 (31ms, the serial-panel catastrophe at grid=2), which is W0's domain. n1024 (Householder 3824us, B=60 only mildly grid-starved and well-optimized) is FAR BELOW the crossover: CQR3 floor ~32ms (measured, min 1-chol config) = ~8x slower. The manager's premise (B=60 -> 10x fewer reortho bmms) does not hold: n1024 matrices are 8x bigger (1024^3) than n512's (512^3) with 10x fewer, so FLOPs are comparable, not 10x less. Fixed overheads at n1024: 2 recursive triinv ~10ms, cuSOLVER cholesky 3.2ms, recon 5.2ms, gate 4.5ms, gram 2ms; even FLOP-optimal ~11-15ms (the x3 multiplier) is still ~3x Householder. Q1 orth after the shifted pass is ~8 (sigma*cond inflation), and there is NO shift giving both a PD tf32x3 Gram AND the Newton-Schulz basin (need 1e-3 < sigma < 2.7e-4, empty), so the globally-convergent chol-reortho's recursive triinv is mandatory. tf32-NS floors orth at ~1.2e-2, right at the n1024 checker gate 1.22e-2 -- too marginal to exploit. CONCLUSION: n1024 is below the CQR-vs-Householder crossover; like n512 it is not winnable with tf32x3 CQR3.
